title: Cranial Nerve Examination: Localizing Common Lesions
subject: Anatomy
preview: Cranial nerve localization combines the pattern of motor, sensory and autonomic deficits rather than one isolated sign.
quickRevision: Cranial nerve localization combines the pattern of motor, sensory and autonomic deficits rather than one isolated sign.
Afferent pupillary light input travels via optic nerve II; efferent constriction travels via oculomotor nerve III.
Bulbar symptoms, diplopia and pupil abnormalities may signal brainstem or compressive disease requiring urgent assessment.

sections.title: Core biomedical mechanism
points: Cranial nerve localization combines the pattern of motor, sensory and autonomic deficits rather than one isolated sign.
A lower motor neuron facial palsy often affects the forehead; typical unilateral supranuclear facial weakness tends to spare forehead movement.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Forehead sparing is a helpful pattern but not an absolute rule in every neurological lesion.
